newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - DEC 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - DEC 30.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Deputy Finance Minister Nikos Christodoulakis is expected to give the sign to the market today for the further reduction of interest rates. At a press conference, Christodoulakis will outline the state's lending policies, aimed at the gradual de-escalation of interest rates so as to reduce the cost of servicing the public debt and to normalise conditions in the market following the decision to levy tax on state titles.
--Insurance firms have made an alternative five-year proposal to bolster the insurance market. The proposal calls on the government to develop a programme to reform ailing insurance firms.
--An IOBE report shows a serious crisis affecting the textile and clothing sectors but the chemicals, non-metals mining and foodstuffs and beverages sectors with favourable prospects.

--The governmet's economic team is expecting favourable developments on the interest rates front in 1997 and is confident that the fall of inflation noted in November will continue this month - nothwithstanding strikes and the 25-day farmers' blockade - to close at 7.5-7.6 percent. Barring any unpleasant surprises, the government hopes to achieve 5.0 percent inflation by the end of the next year.

-- The speedy de-escalation of interest on deposit accounts without a corresponding fall in interest on consumer and business lending and the subsequent increasing divergence in figures is causing concern. Meetings between National Economy and Fionance Minister Yannos Papandoniou and bank administrations early in the New Year will focus on the problem.

--Greece's five private and one state-run casinos recorded turnover of 2.2 billion drachmas in over just two days. Latest figures show gross profits totalling 478 million drachmas with 1997 looking to be even better.

--The Greek telecoms organisation OTE's partial listing on the stock exchange this year injected 96 billion drachmas to the stock exchange, the largets single capital inflow this year. However, without OTE's listing, capital inflows this year were down 15.3 percent over 1995.

--1997 is supposed to be the year that Greece clears its way for its participation in European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU): the government, however, faces serious problems in implementing to the letter the toughest budget in 15 years. Serious problems are expected in convincing the wealthy and affluent to pay new taxes on real estate and state titles, cutting back on public spending and bringing interest rates down by at least two percent.

--Real profits for industries will be lower this year, according to initial estimates: the number of industries showing an improvement in their position on local and international markets has shrunk in relation to 1995, a development that is discouraging for an economy facing the challenge of EMU and modernisation and growth.

--The government is worried at the divergence of economic indicators for 1996 from the targets foreseen in the convergence programme as well as about how to exactly implement the new budget. Movement is expected immediately after the holiday break on four fronts: the state will cut free thousands of state-run bodies and organisations draining the state's coffers; the new bill on health will attempt to better control spending; the moves towards privatisations of state-run banks and ailing firms; and the evaluation of the value of the state's real estate holdings.
--Offers amounting to 2.6 trillion drachmas recorded at Friday's auction of state titles - the last for the year and the last-ever offer of tax-free titles.
